newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen up after PPI figures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen up after PPI figures.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Friday after a weaker-than-forecast report on May U.S. producer prices, analysts said.
"These numbers were materially weaker than was expected," Philip Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's asset management division, said.
"The momentum players will seize this weaker-than-expected PPI number and, in my opinion, continue to drive equity prices higher.

"I don't believe that equity prices are justified where they are currently but this market is working on momentum right now and this indicator is exactly what the momentum guys were hoping for," he added.
The Labor Department reported the Producer Price Index dropped 0.3 percent in May after a 0.6 percent drop in April. Economists in a Reuters poll had expected the PPI to rise 0.1 percent in May.
